---
title: "Multiple variables"
---



Every data variable in the Dataset becomes an `<Array>` in the same VRT,
sharing the dimensions and coordinate arrays.

## Variables in the same files

::: {#952c8b2d .cell execution_count=2}
``` {.python .cell-code}
import xarray as xr
from xvrt import write_mdim_vrt
from _fixtures import daily_netcdf

paths = daily_netcdf(n=3, variables=("sst", "anom", "err"))
ds = xr.open_mfdataset(paths, combine="nested", concat_dim="time")
out = write_mdim_vrt(ds, paths, paths[0].parent / "multi.vrt",
                     composition="concat", concat_dim="time")

from osgeo import gdal
gdal.UseExceptions()
gdal.OpenEx(str(out), gdal.OF_MULTIDIM_RASTER).GetRootGroup().GetMDArrayNames()
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2}
```
['time', 'lat', 'lon', 'sst', 'anom', 'err']
```
:::
:::


- `variables=["sst", "err"]` writes a subset, in that order. By default all
  data variables are written except CF `grid_mapping` containers, whose
  content goes into `<SRS>`.
- Variables without the composition dimension (a static land mask, say) are
  read from the first source.
- `block_size=` takes a dict keyed by variable; a plain list applies only when
  every variable has that rank.
- If the Dataset's names differ from the files', give dict-form sources an
  `"arrays": {"temp": "/sst"}` mapping. A single `"array"` is refused when
  several variables are written, because it would be ambiguous.

## Variables in separate files

Many collections keep each variable in its own file per time step. Pass a
mapping from variable name to its own source list:

::: {#ac14713a .cell execution_count=3}
``` {.python .cell-code}
sst_files = daily_netcdf(n=3, variables=("sst",))
err_files = daily_netcdf(n=3, variables=("err",))
ds = xr.merge([
    xr.open_mfdataset(sst_files, combine="nested", concat_dim="time"),
    xr.open_mfdataset(err_files, combine="nested", concat_dim="time"),
])
out = write_mdim_vrt(ds, {"sst": sst_files, "err": err_files},
                     sst_files[0].parent / "per-variable.vrt",
                     composition="concat", concat_dim="time")
g = gdal.OpenEx(str(out), gdal.OF_MULTIDIM_RASTER).GetRootGroup()
{n: g.OpenMDArray(n).GetDimensions()[0].GetSize() for n in ("sst", "err")}
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=3}
```
{'sst': 3, 'err': 3}
```
:::
:::


Each list is resolved on its own, so lists may differ in length when sources
carry an `"index"` (a variable that starts later, or has missing days): see
[Compositions](compositions.qmd#gaps-placing-sources-by-index) and the
[GHRSST MUR example](../examples/ghrsst-mur.qmd), where one of five variables
exists for only part of the record.
